newsitem.title: USA: FAA proposes limiting B-727 all-cargo weights.
newsitem.headline: FAA proposes limiting B-727 all-cargo weights.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration on Monday proposed limiting the payloads of Boeing 727 aircraft that have been converted from passenger to all-cargo operations.

Operators would have to reduce payloads per container from 8,000 pounds to 3,000 pounds after a final rule is issued until the floor structure is modified or re-qualified to carry greater weight, an FAA statement said.
FAA set a comment period of 45 days and said it expects to issue a final rule by October.
Recent inspections of Boeing 727 cargo interiors revealed that several aircraft contained design features which did not meet FAA certification criteria, FAA said.

"While there has been no failure to date, it is prudent for us to limit the cargo load while corrective modifications are made," said FAA associate administrator for regulation and certification, Guy Gardner.
Payloads up to 4,800 pounds per cargo container would be allowed for up to 120 days after the final rule if the operator met certain FAA restrictions.

FAA said its proposal could affect approximately 300 aircraft worldwide, including 244 U.S. registered aircraft. A total of 32 operators would be affected, including Federal Express Corp, DHL Airways, Express One International, Ryan International Airlines and American International Airways.
FAA said these proposals only addressed the main deck floor structure.

Other modifications would be the subject of a second set of proposals, including designs deviations in cargo door installations, under-strength cargo restraint systems and provision for unauthorized carrying of passengers in cargo areas.
